chunks.title: Landsat Satellite Earth Observation & Surface Temperature
chunks.summary: Landsat Satellite Earth Observation & Surface Temperature by U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) & NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (2022). Standard satellite imagery with a 900 m² (30m × 30m) pixel resolution. Used through automated Google Earth Engine workflows to extract Land Surface Temperature (LST), vegetation cover (NDVI), moisture (NDWI), bare ground (BSI), and built concrete (NDBI). Primarily utilized for campus cooling simulation and tree/misting intervention planning.

chunks.title: NASA POWER / MERRA-2 Satellite Meteorological Reanalysis
chunks.summary: NASA POWER / MERRA-2 Satellite Meteorological Reanalysis by NASA Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO) & Langley Research Center (2024). Supplies all core meteorological weather inputs: solar radiation, air temperature (°C), relative humidity (%), atmospheric pressure, and wind speed. These weather records, combined with LST and NDVI across the entire 3 km² neighborhood polygon, are used to map heat stress (HI_IMD & HHSI) and train the heatwave forecast model.

chunks.title: IMD 5-Tier Heat Hazard Classification & Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
chunks.summary: IMD 5-Tier Heat Hazard Classification & Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) by India Meteorological Department (IMD), Ministry of Earth Sciences, Govt. of India (2023). HI_IMD is calculated to divide the neighborhood into 5 danger categories based on official IMD criteria: Safe/Normal (<32°C), Caution (32–40°C), Extreme Caution (41–46°C), Danger (47–53°C), and Extreme Danger (>54°C). For the Human Heat Stress Index (HHSI), our team incorporated extra demographic vulnerability parameters to assess elevated heat risk for infants below 6 years and elderly citizens above 60 years.

chunks.title: ShadeRoute Multi-Horizon (H0-H3) ML Heatwave Prediction Ensemble
chunks.summary: ShadeRoute Multi-Horizon (H0-H3) ML Heatwave Prediction Ensemble by Team Pipeline Pilots (2026). Operational multi-horizon post-processing model spanning same-day nowcast (H0) through 3-day lead times (H1, H2, H3). Uses a soft-voting ensemble of class-weighted Random Forest (350 trees) and HistGradientBoosting (150 trees) trained on 2022–2024 ERA5/NWP reanalysis with 19 rolling and lagged biometeorological observation features, calibrated decision thresholds (0.35–0.50), and verified against a 2025–2026 out-of-sample temporal holdout (ROC-AUC 0.96–0.97, Accuracy ~95%, Brier score < 0.04).
chunks.text:
[Scientific Source: ShadeRoute Multi-Horizon (H0-H3) ML Heatwave Prediction Ensemble]
Category: Weather, Heat Indices & Forecast
Authors: Team Pipeline Pilots (2026)
Venue: ShadeRoute Machine Learning Pipeline
Role in ShadeRoute: Operational multi-horizon post-processing model spanning same-day nowcast (H0) through 3-day lead times (H1, H2, H3). Uses a soft-voting ensemble of class-weighted Random Forest (350 trees) and HistGradientBoosting (150 trees) trained on 2022–2024 ERA5/NWP reanalysis with 19 rolling and lagged biometeorological observation features, calibrated decision thresholds (0.35–0.50), and verified against a 2025–2026 out-of-sample temporal holdout (ROC-AUC 0.96–0.97, Accuracy ~95%, Brier score < 0.04).
Formula/Mapping: P(Heatwave | NWP_d+h, Obs_Lag, Climatology) = 0.5 * P_RF(x) + 0.5 * P_HGB(x) | Horizon-specific optimal decision thresholds (H0: 0.35, H1: 0.40, H2: 0.50, H3: 0.50) | Ingests live 7-day trailing observations from Open-Meteo
APA Citation: Team Pipeline Pilots. (2026). Multi-horizon ensemble machine learning for urban heatwave nowcasting and short-range prediction: Combining NWP fields with dynamic observational memory. ShadeRoute Technical Report.

chunks.title: ECMWF Integrated Forecasting System (IFS) NWP via Open-Meteo Live API
chunks.summary: ECMWF Integrated Forecasting System (IFS) NWP via Open-Meteo Live API by European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) & Open-Meteo (2024). Supplies live and historical numerical weather prediction (NWP) variables for Bhubaneswar (20.25°N, 85.80°E): surface pressure, precipitation probability, convective showers, CAPE, cloud cover, and wind. Directly feeds the V2 post-processing model and enables detection of rapid barometric pressure drops and convective storm suppression.

chunks.title: Early Detection of Extreme Weather Events via the ECMWF Extreme Forecast Index (EFI)
chunks.summary: Early Detection of Extreme Weather Events via the ECMWF Extreme Forecast Index (EFI) by Zsótér, E. & Lalaurette, F. (2006). Provides the peer-reviewed biometeorological basis for detecting anomalous heatwave conditions against ensemble climatology while factoring in convective instability and barometric pressure drops.
chunks.text:
[Scientific Source: Early Detection of Extreme Weather Events via the ECMWF Extreme Forecast Index (EFI)]
Category: Weather, Heat Indices & Forecast
Authors: Zsótér, E. & Lalaurette, F. (2006)
Venue: Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society, 132(617), 1257–1278
Role in ShadeRoute: Provides the peer-reviewed biometeorological basis for detecting anomalous heatwave conditions against ensemble climatology while factoring in convective instability and barometric pressure drops.
Formula/Mapping: EFI = (2/pi) integral [ (F(x) - F_clim(x)) / sqrt(F_clim(x) * (1 - F_clim(x))) ] dx
APA Citation: Zsótér, E. (2006). Recent developments in extreme weather forecasting: The Extreme Forecast Index. Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society, 132(617), 1257–1278.

chunks.title: Google Earth Engine Automated Spectral Indices & On-Site Tree Ground-Truthing
chunks.summary: Google Earth Engine Automated Spectral Indices & On-Site Tree Ground-Truthing by Google Earth Engine (GEE) Platform & Team Pipeline Pilots Field Inspection (2026). All spectral indices—NDVI (Tree/Plant Canopy), NDWI (Moisture), BSI (Bare Soil), and NDBI (Concrete/Built-up)—were derived directly through automated Google Earth Engine cloud pipelines from Landsat (900 m²) and Sentinel-5P imagery, rather than manual formula calculation. To ground-truth these satellite numbers, our team conducted physical on-site visits across the SOA campus to inspect tree canopy cover, shadow corridors, and open concrete pathways.
chunks.text:
[Scientific Source: Google Earth Engine Automated Spectral Indices & On-Site Tree Ground-Truthing]
Category: Satellite Land & Vegetation Indices
Authors: Google Earth Engine (GEE) Platform & Team Pipeline Pilots Field Inspection (2026)
Venue: Google Earth Engine Automated Pipeline / On-Site Campus Field Survey
Role in ShadeRoute: All spectral indices—NDVI (Tree/Plant Canopy), NDWI (Moisture), BSI (Bare Soil), and NDBI (Concrete/Built-up)—were derived directly through automated Google Earth Engine cloud pipelines from Landsat (900 m²) and Sentinel-5P imagery, rather than manual formula calculation. To ground-truth these satellite numbers, our team conducted physical on-site visits across the SOA campus to inspect tree canopy cover, shadow corridors, and open concrete pathways.
Formula/Mapping: Indices: NDVI = (NIR-Red)/(NIR+Red) | NDBI = (SWIR1-NIR)/(SWIR1+NIR) | BSI = Bare Soil | NDWI = Moisture (Computed automatically in GEE)
APA Citation: Team Pipeline Pilots & Google Earth Engine. (2026). Automated satellite spectral indices and on-site tree canopy ground-truthing survey. ShadeRoute Remote Sensing Documentation.

chunks.title: ExtraTreesRegressor Campus Vegetation Fraction & Priority Intervention Engine
chunks.summary: ExtraTreesRegressor Campus Vegetation Fraction & Priority Intervention Engine by Team Pipeline Pilots (2026). Our final ensemble machine learning regression model (ExtraTreesRegressor, 500 estimators, random_state=2026) trained on 5 spectral and thermal features (NDVI, NDBI, BSI, NDWI, LST). It calculates the continuous vegetation fraction (displayed as Veg% / Tree Cover % in the interface) across all 1,323 sample points of the SOA ITER campus. That predicted vegetation fraction is then directly utilized by the Priority Engine (priority_engine.py) to compute vegetation deficit (weighted at 35%) and recommend targeted cooling interventions: tree planting on open bare zones and misting sprayers along active pedestrian paths.

Authors: Team Pipeline Pilots (2026)

chunks.title: Pedestrian Heat Exposure Index (In-House Scientific Formulation)
chunks.summary: Pedestrian Heat Exposure Index (In-House Scientific Formulation) by Team Pipeline Pilots (Scientific First-Principles Formulation) (2026). Developed in-house by our team because no published journal paper provided an off-the-shelf micro-routing formula for campus footpaths. Grounded in biometeorological first principles: outdoor walking heat strain is a product of ground baking heat (normalized Landsat LST) magnified by the absence of overhead tree shade (1 - NDVI). Where ground surface temperature is hottest and shade is absent, pedestrian danger is maximal.
chunks.text:
[Scientific Source: Pedestrian Heat Exposure Index (In-House Scientific Formulation)]
Category: In-House Scientific Formulas
Authors: Team Pipeline Pilots (Scientific First-Principles Formulation) (2026)
Venue: ShadeRoute Biometeorological Analytical Framework
Role in ShadeRoute: Developed in-house by our team because no published journal paper provided an off-the-shelf micro-routing formula for campus footpaths. Grounded in biometeorological first principles: outdoor walking heat strain is a product of ground baking heat (normalized Landsat LST) magnified by the absence of overhead tree shade (1 - NDVI). Where ground surface temperature is hottest and shade is absent, pedestrian danger is maximal.
Formula/Mapping: Pedestrian Exposure = LST_norm × (1 - NDVI_norm) [In-House First-Principles Formula]
APA Citation: Team Pipeline Pilots. (2026). Pedestrian heat exposure index derived from surface temperature and shade deficit. ShadeRoute Analytical Framework.

chunks.title: Composite Vulnerability Index (VI) (In-House Scientific Formulation)
chunks.summary: Composite Vulnerability Index (VI) (In-House Scientific Formulation) by Team Pipeline Pilots (Scientific Multi-Criteria Formulation) (2026). Formulated in-house by Team Pipeline Pilots to quantify neighborhood vulnerability across the 3 km² study zone. It combines three logical, evidence-based pillars: (1) Density of populations most vulnerable to heatstroke (infants under 6 years and senior citizens over 60 years), (2) Proximity to emergency hospitals and schools, and (3) Lack of cooling tree canopy.
chunks.text:
[Scientific Source: Composite Vulnerability Index (VI) (In-House Scientific Formulation)]
Category: In-House Scientific Formulas
Authors: Team Pipeline Pilots (Scientific Multi-Criteria Formulation) (2026)

Role in ShadeRoute: Formulated in-house by Team Pipeline Pilots to quantify neighborhood vulnerability across the 3 km² study zone. Formula/Mapping: VI = 0.455·PopRisk(<6y & >60y) + 0.364·FacilityProximity + 0.181·CanopyDeficit [In-House Formula]
APA Citation: Team Pipeline Pilots. (2026). Multi-criteria demographic and spatial heat vulnerability index. ShadeRoute Analytical Framework.

chunks.title: Dual-Metric Probability of Precipitation (PoP) & Diurnal Areal Averaging
chunks.summary: Dual-Metric Probability of Precipitation (PoP) & Diurnal Areal Averaging by World Meteorological Organization (WMO No. 488) & US National Weather Service (NWS) (2023). Underpins ShadeRoute's Dual-Metric Precipitation Framework: (1) Standard Daily PoP (49% on Sep 14) aligns with WMO standard 12-hour/24-hour diurnal ensemble probability (matching MSN Weather, IMD, and AccuWeather reports); (2) Hourly NWP Convective Peak (97% at 15:00 IST) resolves acute afternoon cloudburst timing to detect convective thermal suppression and localized flood/humidity surges.
chunks.text:
[Scientific Source: Dual-Metric Probability of Precipitation (PoP) & Diurnal Areal Averaging]
Category: Weather, Heat Indices & Forecast
Authors: World Meteorological Organization (WMO No. 488) & US National Weather Service (NWS) (2023)
Venue: WMO Manual on the Global Data-processing and Forecasting System & NWS Instruction 10-503
Role in ShadeRoute: Underpins ShadeRoute's Dual-Metric Precipitation Framework: (1) Standard Daily PoP (49% on Sep 14) aligns with WMO standard 12-hour/24-hour diurnal ensemble probability (matching MSN Weather, IMD, and AccuWeather reports); (2) Hourly NWP Convective Peak (97% at 15:00 IST) resolves acute afternoon cloudburst timing to detect convective thermal suppression and localized flood/humidity surges.
Formula/Mapping: Daily PoP = (Daytime_Mean + 24h_Mean) / 2 [Standard Channel Alignment] | Hourly Peak = max(hourly_PoP)
APA Citation: World Meteorological Organization. (2023). Guide to the global data-processing and forecasting system (WMO-No. 488). WMO Press.

chunks.summary: IMD Automated Weather Station (AWS) Network & Monsoon Heat-Humidity Surveillance by India Meteorological Department (IMD), Regional Meteorological Centre, Bhubaneswar (2024). Localized micro-climate phenomena (convective thunderstorm cells, sea-breeze penetration, asphalt heat retention) may exhibit temporal or spatial variance from NWP grid outputs. Precipitation probabilities display peak hourly precipitation probability for convective timing.

Individual heat tolerance varies significantly with age, cardiovascular fitness, hydration, medications, and pre-existing chronic illnesses (COPD, diabetes, kidney disease). Pedestrians, students, and campus visitors are advised to heed official IMD color-coded heat warnings, maintain adequate hydration, avoid direct sun exposure during peak thermal hours, and seek immediate medical attention at the SOA Dispensary or IMS & SUM Hospital if experiencing symptoms of heat exhaustion or heatstroke.

chunks.title: ShadeRoute V2 Multi-Horizon ML Heatwave Ensemble Model
chunks.summary: Soft-voting ensemble of RandomForest and HistGradientBoosting predicting H0 nowcast to H3 lead times.
chunks.text:
[ShadeRoute Machine Learning: Heatwave Ensemble Model]
Architecture: Soft-voting ensemble combining class-weighted RandomForest (350 trees) and HistGradientBoosting (150 trees).
Lead Horizons: Same-day nowcast (H0), 1-day ahead (H1), 2-day ahead (H2), and 3-day ahead (H3) heatwave probability.
Inputs: Live Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) feeds from ECMWF Integrated Forecasting System (IFS) and Open-Meteo, 7-day lagged biometeorological observation history, diurnal solar geometry, barometric pressure rate of change, and convective storm proxy (CAPE).
Performance: ROC-AUC 0.96-0.97, Accuracy ~95%, Brier score < 0.04 across 2025-2026 holdout verification.

chunks.title: Pedestrian Corridors Planting Priority & Misting Engine
chunks.summary: Priority engine placing up to 400 shade trees and 100 high-pressure mist sprayers along high-heat pedestrian paths.
chunks.text:
[ShadeRoute Campus Cooling Interventions: Trees & Mist Sprayers]
Scope: 10m x 10m high-resolution walkway grid connecting hostels, lecture halls, auditoriums, and cafeterias across the SOA ITER campus.
Shade Trees Intervention: Up to 400 shade trees placed at critical pedestrian corridors. Tree canopies intercept solar radiation and cool ground surface temperatures by up to ~4°C through natural leaf evapotranspiration.
Mist Sprayers Intervention: Up to 100 high-pressure evaporative mist nozzles placed along student corridors. Flash evaporation of micro-droplets absorbs ambient sensible heat, dropping perceived "feels-like" temperature by up to ~2°C.
Optimization: Evaluates Land Surface Temperature (LST), Bare Soil Index (BSI), lack of canopy (NDVI deficit), and pedestrian walking density to pinpoint maximum-benefit locations.

chunks.title: Hospital Patient Surge & Clinical Resource Readiness Model

chunks.text:
[Hospital Surge & Clinical Readiness Model]
Methodology: Epidemiology-grounded deterministic decision support calibrated for 4 healthcare facilities near SOA ITER (SOA Student Health Centre, IMS & SUM Hospital, AIIMS Bhubaneswar, AMRI Hospital).
Standards: Grounded in NCDC National Action Plan on Heat-Related Illnesses (NAP-HRI 2024), AIIMS Emergency Medicine protocols, WHO heat-health guidance (2024), and Distributed Lag Non-Linear Models (DLNM).
Resource Allocation: Forecasts patient influx, dedicated Heat Stroke Units (HSUs, 20% of excess admissions), ORS solution packets, chilled IV crystalloid fluids (3.5L per patient), and emergency cooling beds.

chunks.title: Satellite Remote Sensing & Multispectral Indices (10m Spatial Grid)
chunks.summary: Ingests Landsat 8/9, Sentinel-2, and Sentinel-5P via Google Earth Engine for LST, NDVI, NDBI, NDWI, and BSI.
chunks.text:
[Satellite Remote Sensing Specifications]
Spatial Grid: 10m x 10m grid covering SOA ITER campus and 3 km² neighborhood.
Sensors: Landsat 8/9 TIRS-2, Sentinel-2 MSI, and Sentinel-5P TROPOMI processed through Google Earth Engine (GEE).
Computed Indices: Land Surface Temperature (LST), Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI, tree canopy), Normalized Difference Built-up Index (NDBI, concrete), Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI, surface moisture), Bare Soil Index (BSI), and continuous vegetation fraction.

chunks.title: IMD Heat Danger Alert Levels & Visual Map Color Legend
chunks.summary: Five-tier IMD heat hazard color code: Red (Urgent Danger), Orange (High Concern), Yellow (Moderate), Green (Safe), Blue (Cool).
chunks.text:
[Map Colors & IMD Heat Danger Alert Levels]
Red (🔴 Urgent Danger): Severe heat stress zones lacking tree shade with blistering ground surface heat (>54°C HI). Immediate planting or misting intervention needed.
Orange (🟠 High Concern / Alert): Elevated thermal risk during afternoon peak hours (47-53°C HI). High risk of dehydration and heat exhaustion.
Yellow (🟡 Moderate Concern / Watch): Noticeable warmth (41-46°C HI); caution and adequate hydration advised.
Green (🟢 Safe / Normal): Comfortable ambient conditions (<40°C HI).
Blue (🔵 Very Cool): Well-shaded canopy corridors, vegetated parks, or active evaporative misting zones.
